question: Would keeping airport metadata between client sessions reduce repeated lookup requests?
workload: One fictional two-leg trip visiting the same two airports. Clear process memory between legs. Each leg requests a name and a timezone for both airports.

alternatives.name: Persistent airport metadata cache
alternatives.cost: Forecast two transport requests across the trip at an illustrative USD 0.015 per request.
alternatives.quality: All four name and timezone pairs should agree with the reference data. Refresh the metadata after seven days.

alternatives.name: Memory-only cache
alternatives.cost: Forecast four transport requests at the same illustrative price.
alternatives.quality: The same four pairs should agree. Each restarted process has to look up the airports again.

evidence.finding: Two airports recur immediately. There are no metadata changes, retries, or credits in this example.

recommendation: Keep reference metadata on disk across both legs.
reversal_condition: Revisit the cache policy when stale results require frequent corrections or the request pattern changes.
missing: Field freshness and effective billed cost in an actual deployment.
